<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Plan 075 gave `harness commit` a fourth branch (`ingress-unverified`, the Windows named pipe) and updated the instructions page to describe it. It did NOT update the managed `AGENTS.md` block, which still promises exactly two outcomes: a confirmed note, or a named buffer plus the nudge that drains it. On Windows an agent is therefore told to expect an outcome it cannot get, and is pointed at a recovery command that refuses on that platform.

The text fix is one paragraph. The DEFECT is that the outcome contract exists in two hand-maintained prose copies with nothing forcing them to agree — so it drifted once and will drift again at the next branch change. This plan converges both surfaces on a single table keyed by `CommitMode`, so a fifth mode cannot be added without the guidance failing to compile. That is the house pattern already proven twice: `TRACE2_TARGET_POLICY` (ingress.ts) and `RETAINED_FIELD_RENDERING` (nudge.ts).

This is the same failure this family of plans exists to kill — a surface claiming more than the code delivers — reappearing one layer up, in the documentation OF the safeguard.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- The managed block names every outcome an agent can actually receive from `harness commit`, including the named-pipe path where attribution is unverified and the nudge must NOT be run.
- The outcome contract lives in ONE exported table keyed by `CommitMode`, and both guidance surfaces render from it — no second hand-maintained prose copy of the outcome list.
- Adding a fifth `CommitMode` is a COMPILE ERROR at the guidance surface, not a review catch. A guarantee about future code needs the type system, not a test (DL-007).
- Repos carrying the old block migrate gracefully: it reads as `stale`, doctor warns, and `harness instructions commit --inject` refreshes it in place.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing commit BEHAVIOUR. Not one branch of `commit-service.ts` moves; this plan changes what the guidance SAYS about branches that already exist.
- Windows replay support. Still blocked on the unverified transport premise — nobody has run `git config --global --get trace2.eventTarget` on a Windows box.
- Editing `AGENTS.md` outside the managed markers, in this repo or any other. The block owns the region between its fences and nothing else.
- A `windows-latest` CI leg. Approved by prime, but it belongs to issue #108's PR under that ruling's same-PR-and-green condition — not here.
- Rewording the instructions page's prose beyond what deriving it from the table requires.
